blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A supply chain is a group of players. Each one does a different job. The supplier provides the raw materials. The manufacturer turns these materials into products.

The distributor moves the products to the right places. The retailer sells them in a shop. The customer buys and uses them. No single player controls everything. They all depend on each other.

When one player fails, the others notice quickly. So knowing who does what is the first step to working well with any of them.

items.q: Who provides the raw materials?
items.why: "The supplier provides the raw materials."

items.q: What does the manufacturer do?
options: It turns raw materials into products
It buys and uses the products
It sells products in a shop
items.why: "The manufacturer turns these materials into products."

items.q: The text says the players "all depend on each other." This suggests that…
options: One player can do all the jobs alone
No player really needs the others
Each player needs the other players to work
The customer is not part of the chain
items.why: Inferência: "depend on each other" quer dizer que um precisa do outro para funcionar.

items.q: Which idea would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: It helps to know who does what
Each player does a different job
One player controls the whole chain
When one player fails, the others notice fast
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "No single player controls everything" — o autor discorda dessa ideia.

items.q: Why is it useful to know who does what?
options: To work well with each player
items.why: "knowing who does what is the first step to working well with any of them."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver falando com um novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Today I want to show you the players on one product line. Let's start at the top.

First, we have our supplier. This company gives us the raw materials — the coffee and the sugar. They are very good, but sometimes they are late.

Next is the manufacturer. They take the raw materials and make the final product. After that, the distributor moves the boxes from the factory to the shops. This part is important. If the trucks stop, the shops have nothing to sell.

Then we have the retailer. This is the shop. They sell the product to the customer, the person who buys it and uses it at home.

Here is the key point for you. Every player depends on the others. When the supplier is late, the manufacturer waits. When the manufacturer waits, the shop is empty. So watch the whole chain, not just one part. When you see a problem early, you can fix it fast.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does the supplier give the team?
options: The raw materials, like coffee and sugar
items.why: "our supplier… gives us the raw materials — the coffee and the sugar."

items.q: What does the distributor do?
options: It moves the boxes from the factory to the shops
items.why: "the distributor moves the boxes from the factory to the shops."

items.q: Oliver says, "If the trucks stop, the shops have nothing to sell." This suggests that…
options: The shops make their own products
The distributor's job is not important
The shops need the distributor to bring the products
items.why: Inferência: sem os caminhões (distribuidor), a loja fica sem produto para vender.

items.q: Why does Oliver tell the analyst to watch the whole chain?
options: Because the customer is not important
Because one problem can affect all the players
items.why: Inferência: ele explica que um atraso passa de um player para o outro, então é preciso olhar tudo.

items.q: Who is the customer in Oliver's talk?
options: The company that sends raw materials
The factory that makes the product
The person who buys and uses the product at home
items.why: "the customer, the person who buys it and uses it at home."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our best supplier sends us fresh coffee every week." A supplier is a company that…
items.why: Supplier = fornecedor: quem fornece materiais ou mercadorias.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ turns the raw sugar into small packets."
items.why: Manufacturer = fabricante: quem transforma a matéria-prima em produto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ moves the boxes from the factory to many shops."
items.why: Distributor = distribuidor: quem leva os produtos aos pontos de venda.

items.q: "Steel and cotton are common raw materials." Raw materials are…
options: basic materials used to make products
items.why: Raw material = matéria-prima: o material básico usado para fazer os produtos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Each player depends ___ the others to keep the chain moving."
items.why: "depend on" = depender de. A preposição correta é "on".

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the new supplier." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new product to the shops next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, colocar em operação (aos poucos ou por etapas).

items.q: "When the trucks are late, we need to sort out the problem fast." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, arrumar um problema.

items.q: "Our supplier sometimes runs out of boxes." To run out of something means to…
items.why: Run out of = ficar sem, acabar o estoque de algo.

items.q: "If one player is slow, it can hold up the whole chain." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, segurar o andamento de algo.
